Tuatara's, a primitive lizard like animal that exists in New Zealand, have three "eyes". The one on the top of the head is called a parietal eye which senses light but is not actually involved in producing a visual sense. It is attached to the pineal gland and is involved in hormone regulation of the circadian rhythm. Since almost every vertebrate species has a pineal gland, a third eye on a catfish is probably the result of the accidental expression of genes that were important in the catfish's ancestors that are suppressed in the modern day version of the animal.
